name: RIGHT
description: RIGHT returns the last character(s) from the end of a text string.
tldr: RIGHT extracts a specified number of characters from the right side of a text string.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The text string from which to extract characters.

parameters.name: num_chars
parameters.description: Optional. The number of characters to extract (default is 1).

basicExample.explanation: Extracts the last 4 characters from "Hello World".

advancedExamples.title: Extract file extension
advancedExamples.description: Get the extension from a filename
advancedExamples.explanation: Combines RIGHT with LEN and FIND to extract text after the dot.

advancedExamples.title: Extract last name
advancedExamples.description: Get the last name from "First Last" format
advancedExamples.explanation: Extracts text after the first space.

howItWorks: RIGHT counts from the end of the text string and returns the specified number of characters. If num_chars is omitted, it returns just the last character.

howToSteps.name: Select output cell
howToSteps.text: Choose where the result should appear.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The result shows the extracted text.

limitations: RIGHT counts each character as 1, including spaces.
Use LEFT to extract from the beginning, or MID to extract from the middle.

commonErrors.fix: Ensure num_chars is a positive number.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: RIGHT works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: Does RIGHT work with numbers?
faq.answer: Yes, numbers are treated as text.

faq.question: What if num_chars exceeds the text length?
faq.answer: RIGHT returns the entire text string.
